title: Product users created without a status were stored and returned as ACTIVE, outside the contract enum
summary: Since the v1 snapshot (2026-05-11), `POST /v1/products/{id}/product-users` without `status` stored the user as `ACTIVE` and answered `"status": "ACTIVE"`, although the contract enum is `active`, `invited`, `suspended`. Every Clerk-synced user was stored the same way. A `statuses: ["active"]` search does not match those rows, and a client that decodes the enum strictly cannot read the response. The flow suite found it on 2026-11-04 at 00:13Z, when an email-only create added to `anchor: product-user` after anchor#321 got `ACTIVE` back. The fix stores and returns the contract spelling, backfills stored rows (migration 000074), ignores the letter case of a requested status, validates it against the enum in the service, and fails a read of a stored value outside the enum. It waits for human review because it changes a visible response.

impact.text: Prod and dev, every product. Responses for default and Clerk-synced users carry a value outside the documented enum, and status searches with the documented values miss those users. The number of affected clients is unknown: nothing logs enum mismatches. This is the same class as the 2026-10-26 name contract drift.

tests that created a user without a status

trigger: The routine's email-only create in `anchor: product-user` (run 01a1a3e7, 00:13:56Z) asserted `$.status` equals `active` and got `ACTIVE`; the same flow's creates that send `status: active` get `active` back.
detection: Detected by a new flow check written from the contract, not from observed responses, while the routine updated the check for anchor#321. No test, alert or customer report had shown it in six months.
resolution: Not resolved on dev or prod yet. The fix, anchor#PRNUM, supersedes anchor#323 (it adds the backfill and the strict read). It passes the unit, repository, service and CT suites and the golden contract suite locally, and waits for review. The reproduction moved to `anchor: known bugs`; the gate flow no longer asserts the default status.

whys.problem: Clients get `status: ACTIVE`, outside the documented enum, and status searches miss those users

because.text: A create without `status` defaulted to the domain constant `ACTIVE` and the response cast it unchanged
The domain and the contract spell statuses differently, and the API converts between them with a type cast
because.evidence: Domain `ACTIVE`/`INACTIVE` vs contract `active`/`invited`/`suspended`; Clerk upsert also writes `ACTIVE`

because.text: Enum values are declared twice (domain and contract) with no single source or mapping test
No test ever created a user without a status, so the default path never met an assertion
because.evidence: CT DSL `product_links_builder.go` sends `ACTIVE`; #321's email-only CT sends `status: active`; every flow create sent a status

because.text: The shared create helpers fill every optional field so one helper serves every test
because.evidence: `createDSLProductUser` always sends name and status; flows copied full bodies

because.text: Create tests send convenient bodies, not the contract's minimum body; this is open action A2 of the 2026-10-26 postmortem
Nothing flagged the value for six months
Responses are not checked against the OpenAPI schema in CTs, and requests with `ACTIVE` passed validation too
because.evidence: The DSL's `ACTIVE` create returns 201 on main; CT asserts compare to generated constants only

because.text: Neither CTs nor the server validate responses (and request enums) against openapi.yaml
Stored rows mix `ACTIVE` and `active`, so the fix backfills them and reads any letter case while replicas of the previous release still write `ACTIVE`
The service accepted any status string: the create input validated `required` only, and the request validator let `ACTIVE` through
because.evidence: `CreateProductUserInput.Status validate:"required"`; the CT DSL's `ACTIVE` create answers 201

because.text: Status writes had no enum validation in the service layer, which owns business rules in Anchor

contributing: Clerk upsert compares `existing.Status != ACTIVE`, so a user created through the API with `active` counted as changed on every sync.
The 2026-10-26 postmortem's contract-minimum action was still open.

well: Writing the new check from the contract, not from the observed response, found the bug at once.
The fix keeps clients that send `ACTIVE` working by folding the case instead of refusing them.
wrong: The same class of drift was found nine days earlier and its prevention action is still open.
#321 fixed the name default but its CT still sent a status, so the minimum body stayed untested.
lucky: The bug surfaced only because the gate check for #321 needed rewriting that night; the default path had no other test.

A one-time backfill (migration 000074, allowed by `-- lint: allow-backfill`) moves stored rows to the contract spelling. The read ignores letter case only for the deploy window, and a follow-up removes that.

actions.what: Store and return contract statuses, backfill stored rows, fold input case, validate the enum in the service, reject unknown stored values
CT per create operation with only the contract's required fields, asserting every defaulted field
Validate CT responses against openapi.yaml (kin-openapi response validation in the CT client)
Known-bugs reproduction; move into `anchor: product-user` once the fix is live
flow-suite-testing skill: a create check sends only required fields and asserts each default against the contract

messaging.internal: Anchor returns product user status ACTIVE for users created without a status and for Clerk-synced users; the contract says active. Fix waiting for review.
messaging.external: Product users created without a status, and users synced from Clerk, were returned with status ACTIVE instead of active. Responses now use the documented values, and searches by status find these users.
